key_idea: A random set is exposed in small rounds. In each round, the spread condition lets every remaining edge S∖W be replaced by a much smaller minimal edge it contains, and a split into pathological and nonpathological configurations sharpens the counting so that the extra log factor disappears.
reason: The iterative shrinking argument is short and conceptually clear: spreadness makes the leftover parts of edges shrink geometrically, and Janson's inequality finishes off the small final stage. These ideas make the bound feel inevitable. Some bookkeeping remains in the main lemma's two-part counting and in the parameter tuning (and Theorem 7 adds a further case split), so the proof falls short of a 'book proof'.
recognized: Park–Pham, 'A proof of the Kahn–Kalai conjecture' (fractional expectation-threshold version, building on Frankston–Kahn–Narayanan–Park)
